Results report stereotactic coordinates for activation peaks (e.g., anterior striatum, midbrain, rLPFC) and reference supplementary tables; BOLD responses were modeled and analyzed. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are presented and small-volume corrections are reported, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes within-healthy-group task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving (arithmetic word problems requiring a goal and steps to reach it). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants (n=36 analyzed), with voxelwise results reported in MNI stereotactic space (coordinate tables/figures) using SPM8. The paper includes whole-brain statistical thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and reports task-related BOLD increases. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using a representation-matching task (goal-directed comparison of symbolic equations and charts, including a condition requiring calculation), which qualifies as a problem-solving task under the review definition. It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (two-sample t-tests) on healthy adult participants, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). All required voxelwise results are reported. No exclusion criteria were met: results are not ROI-only, participants are healthy adults, and the study is empirical. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content is complete.

Excluded because this is a single-subject (n=1) case study of a 16-year-old abacus expert; no group-level healthy adult whole-brain fMRI effects are reported. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect / only single-subject). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of a mental addition task which meets a goal-directed computation), I7 (reports stereotactic normalization to MNI space and lists coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported and available). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (requires at least one whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adult individuals) — not satisfied because only one adolescent subject and no group-level statistics. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving/fluid reasoning task), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) and group-level within-group effects reported for the healthy comparison group. BOLD-based analyses and psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results are reported. The manuscript indicates stereotactic peak coordinates were identified (seed coordinates and peak activations) and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Note: sample age range (14–36) includes some adolescents, and exact coordinate values are not shown in the provided excerpt, so confidence is moderate.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. While it is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates in healthy adult controls (I7, I8) and reporting voxelwise results in the main text (I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (mental rotation is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm) (I5 not met). Additionally, all reported fMRI analyses were hypothesis-driven ROI (small-volume) analyses rather than unbiased whole-brain group-level analyses (I6 not met), triggering exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a math calculation task (goal-directed computation) fitting the problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses and voxelwise results with MNI stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD (fMRI) activation contrasts are presented (tables/figures and ROI follow-ups). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it satisfies I5–I9.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal followed by a need to figure out a way to reach it). It examines social truth-telling and evaluative judgments (social vs simple truth questions) rather than problem-solving across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem solving). No exclusion criteria were triggered (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial reasoning (a problem-solving task with goal and steps), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=20). The study reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (GLM, group-level contrast maps) with normalization to MNI space and identifies ROIs based on group contrasts; BOLD fMRI was used. Coordinates/activation maps are reported/indicated. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines clinical reasoning (MCQ diagnosis task) which is a problem-solving task (goal: determine diagnosis; requires devising a way to reach it). It uses task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level AFNI 3dttest++), reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates and t/p values for task-related activation and covariates, and presents BOLD (percent-change) results corrected for multiple comparisons. Participants are healthy adult physicians (residents and faculty). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reports task-related activations in MNI space using BOLD contrast (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9). However, the experimental tasks are rhyme judgment (language) and mental rotation (spatial visualization), which are perceptual/processing tasks and do not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Therefore the paper does not address problem-solving across domains as required and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

The study uses a task-based BOLD fMRI Tower of London (ToL) planning paradigm, which is a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning). It reports whole-brain, group-level effects for the ToL (main effect of increasing task load) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for task-related activations (e.g., left medial dorsolateral PFC: x=-27 y=30 z=24 for interaction). The sample includes healthy adult participants (controls) and the reported task activations are derived from group-level second-level analyses that include healthy adults. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis including healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinates/results available within text/tables/analyses). Although the sample also includes MDD patients, the presence of healthy adults and whole-brain task effects makes this eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving (a bona fide problem-solving task). It includes longitudinal and cross-sectional whole-brain analyses with group-level effects that include a healthy adult group (n=20) and reports whole-brain contrasts (addition vs control) using stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation peaks. The paper reports BOLD fMRI results and voxelwise analyses (whole-brain and searchlight/multivoxel), with coordinates provided in the main text and figures. It is not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, and includes within-group task effects for healthy adults. The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=42) using BOLD fMRI during mental arithmetic tasks (multiplication and subtraction), which qualify as problem-solving (goal-directed computation). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes voxelwise results presented in tables/figures as well as ROI analyses. All required criteria are met: task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task (I5), whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), coordinates in MNI space (I7), BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and reporting of voxelwise coordinate results in main text/figures (I9). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation including a mental calculation task (silent subtraction), which meets the review definition of a problem-solving task (goal: compute result; requires figuring out procedure). It reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses on 81 healthy adult subjects, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (3T EPI) with voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results) — the authors conducted ROI-based analyses and explicitly state a whole-brain approach was not used; E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect) — the analysis uses extant fMRI datasets drawn from participants with Williams syndrome only (no healthy adult group-level task effects are reported for the current analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analyses) — the study uses fMRI BOLD measures. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task; tasks are passive listening/viewing with low cognitive load), I6 (does not include whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for whole-brain task effects in healthy adults), I9 (no voxelwise whole-brain results reported for healthy adults). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study of propositional analogical reasoning (a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task) that includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript presents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and multiple regression results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., left RLPFC at −27, 50, 0; right RLPFC at 27, 45, 16), and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are reported across whole-brain maps and ROI follow-ups; they are not limited to ROI-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a syllogistic deductive-reasoning task. The reasoning task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (participants have the goal of deciding whether a conclusion follows and must determine how to reach that decision). The study reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM8), reports stereotactic MNI coordinates in the text and supplementary tables/figures, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Voxelwise results are reported in supplementary tables and main text figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n≈15 in imaging analyses) using a reasoning task (syllogistic inference) where participants had the explicit goal to judge whether a conclusion follows from premises (i.e., goal-directed computation fitting the provided problem-solving definition). Group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported with stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations and interaction contrasts. BOLD (fMRI) analyses are used and voxelwise results are reported in the main text and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, participants are healthy adults, task effects within the healthy group are reported, and the paper is empirical with original data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses the Tower of London (ToL) planning task, which qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (I5), and it reports stereotactic coordinates (I7) from BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) with coordinates available in the text (I9). However, it does not present a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for healthy adults relevant to problem-solving. The reported imaging results focus on genotype-related correlations and diagnosis-by-genotype interactions (including ROI-based PFC findings) rather than reporting whole-brain task-related group effects in the healthy control group. The authors report that no other areas emerged as significant in whole-brain analyses for the ToL, and the principal ToL effects appear to be reported within an ROI framework. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (doesn't include healthy-group task effects/only between-group/genotype contrasts relevant to this review). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental paradigm is multiple object tracking (MOT) investigating sensorimotor prediction/attention, not a problem-solving task as defined (a task with an explicit goal plus a need to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (compound remote associate problems) in healthy adults, using whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis reporting BOLD results. The paper reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., peak at 44, -9, -9) and describes whole-brain cluster-thresholding procedures. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult novice participants performing a multiple-choice electric-circuit task that requires judging correctness (a goal-directed problem-solving/decision task). The study reports whole-brain group-level SPM analyses on BOLD data, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates and tables/figures of task-related activations, and voxelwise results are reported. All inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (it includes group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is a similarity-judgment/working-memory labeling task, not a problem-solving task as defined by a goal plus needing to figure out a way to reach it) and I7 (the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space for task-related activations in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults with group-level random effects analyses and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results. However, it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined (a task that first has a goal and then requires figuring out a way to reach it). Instead, participants made communicative/strategic vs control judgments about social scenarios (moral/communication evaluation), which is not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text unavailable (only title/metadata provided). Cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / could not be confirmed: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting in Talairach/MNI), I8 (BOLD or rCBF analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results availability). No exclusion criteria met based on available information. Full text is incomplete, so study must be excluded until full text is obtained for assessment.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing single-digit multiplication problems (a problem-solving task). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, including contrasts of interest (large vs. small problems) and inter-group comparisons. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and derive from BOLD fMRI analyses; voxelwise cluster results are presented (tables/figures). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an arithmetic problem-solving task in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses and BOLD contrasts reported, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic peak coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the main text. While ROI center coordinates (from a meta-analysis) and references to Figures/Tables are present, explicit voxelwise peak coordinates for the reported activations are not shown in the provided material. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinate results) and cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used an N-Back working memory task (a continuous performance/working memory paradigm), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring figuring out a way to reach a goal). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study with group analyses, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt, and the task domain does not match the meta-analysis target (problem solving). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the review.

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The experiments are categorical and coordinate spatial judgment tasks (perceptual/decision tasks) rather than problem-solving paradigms that require setting a goal and devising a means/strategy to reach it. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses reported), I7 (results/methods report MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI reported), and I9 (voxelwise/ROI and whole-brain results are described and available). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3, E4, E5, E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails the essential inclusion criterion I5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using BOLD contrast in healthy adult participants (20 licensed taxi drivers). The task is goal-directed navigation delivering customers to destinations, requiring subjects to plan routes and solve problems in real-time, meeting the definition of a problem-solving task (goal plus need to figure out a way to reach it). The analysis is whole-brain (SPM2 preprocessing and random-effects second-level t-tests), reporting stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise results (tables/figures) for task-related increases. Thus it satisfies I5–I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded (E3): The study reports PET results using predefined ROI analyses (regional binding potentials) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis. Inclusion met: I5 — it is a task-based PET study using an attentive calculation task (problem-focused calculation) in healthy adults. Inclusion NOT met: I6 — no whole-brain voxelwise/group-level whole-brain analysis is reported; I7 — no stereotactic (Talairach/MNI) coordinate results are provided; I8 — the outcomes are PET receptor binding potentials (BP) for H1 receptors, not task-related BOLD or rCBF measures. Full text appears complete. Based on these, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, it does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates category-based induction and the inclusion fallacy — a comparative semantic/reasoning judgment about which of two inductive arguments is stronger — rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm that requires establishing a goal and figuring out means to achieve it (e.g., planning, multi-step solution search). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=11, mean age 26.9) using auditory multidigit addition (a goal-directed problem-solving task) with blocked task blocks. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates normalized to MNI space (with supplementary tables/figures reporting task-related activations). All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, includes within-healthy-group task effects). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on these factors, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults performing a simple mental calculation (X×Y+Z), so it meets I5 (task with a goal needing a method), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the manuscript or tables; activations are shown as figures/voxel maps but no coordinates are provided, so it fails I7 and I9. Because reporting of standardized coordinates is required for inclusion in this coordinate-based meta-analysis, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results as stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for group-level effects. However, the experimental task investigates humor comprehension/incongruity resolution (reading/verbal jokes) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (having a goal and needing to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met). It is a methods/rtfMRI validation study using a finger-tapping motor task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/activation maps indicated in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I7 (the full text does not clearly present stereotactic coordinate tables of task-related increases in Talairach/MNI space). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because participants are adolescents (mean ages 16.8 and 16.9), not healthy adults as required by inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI mental-rotation task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition), I7 (task-related stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires healthy adult participants; sample is adolescent). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the report. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This is a behavioral study of arithmetic (reaction times and strategy ratings) in healthy adults; it does not include any task-based fMRI or PET data, whole-brain group-level analyses, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results. Full text is complete. Exclusion rationale: No imaging modalities or voxelwise results reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analysis), I9 (not applicable—no voxelwise results to report). Exclusion criteria met: none of the listed exclusion IDs (E3–E6) directly apply; exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving studies.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task = mental calculation, a problem-solving-like task with goal and method), I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI was performed in nine healthy adults), I8 (fMRI BOLD sequence and task-related fMRI analysis were reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (the paper does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space — no coordinate tables or coordinate reporting are present in the full text provided), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results are reported in tables, figures, or supplements as required). Because I7 (and I9) are required and are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a modified beads (probabilistic reasoning) task where participants have the goal (identify lake source) and must determine how to reach it (decide how many samples to draw) — meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and event-related contrasts in healthy adults, with stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations (e.g., VTA [3 −25 −11], VS [12 8 −8]) and reports BOLD fMRI results. Results are presented in the main text with coordinates and ROI analyses supplementing whole-brain findings. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based BOLD fMRI of healthy adults during a probabilistic inference (jumping-to-conclusions) task, so it meets I5 (task involves a goal and iterative evidence-gathering to reach it) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). However, the paper reports ROI-based multivariate analyses (DLPFC, ACC, OFC, hippocampus, etc.) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis with stereotactic coordinates. No Talairach/MNI coordinate tables or whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are provided in the full text. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results) and does not meet inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis) or I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates). I9 (availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplement) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based primarily on E3 plus failure to meet I6 and I7.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16) that examines analogical reasoning requiring subjects to generate representations and map source to target to choose a correct target (i.e., a goal-directed problem-solving process). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, reports task-related BOLD effects, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (multiple BA10 peaks and other regions). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based neuroimaging studies of problem solving (I5–I9). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement learning) task rather than an explicit problem-solving task. While the task involves obtaining rewards and adapting behavior, it primarily probes model-free/model-based learning and prediction error signaling, not higher-order problem solving or planning per se. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results referenced in main/supplementary materials). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task does not clearly constitute a problem-solving task as defined—having a goal and requiring subjects to figure out a way to reach it in the sense of complex problem solving across domains). No exclusion criteria were directly triggered (e.g., results are not ROI-only, the sample is healthy adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5.

This study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving as defined by the review (I5 not met). It instead investigates theory-of-mind processes (cooperation vs. deception) using cartoon stories requiring belief/intention attribution, not tasks with an explicit goal and requirement to figure out a way to reach it. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults; n=13, random-effects analyses), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates / peak voxels; MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (task-related voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used BOLD imaging and whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects GLM). Participants performed spatial memory/imagery tasks (REF, ROT, JRD) that require an explicit goal (point to a cued object) and transformation/mental-reasoning to determine the response, meeting the review definition of problem solving (goal plus need to figure out how to reach it). The functional data were normalized to Talairach space and the manuscript reports task-related activations with referenced tables/figures of voxelwise stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a number-series reasoning task (a problem-solving task: goal-directed rule discovery and solution). It includes whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (task-related contrasts EASY/DIFFICULT > CONTROL), reports MNI-normalized results and cluster activations, and uses BOLD-fMRI. Voxelwise results are presented in whole-brain analyses and figures/tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, analyses), Results (behavioral and whole-brain activation), and Discussion; full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and group-level voxelwise analyses. However, the tasks (serial order STM recognition, alphabetical order judgments, numerical order comparisons, and luminance judgments) probe ordinal/sequence processing and short-term memory, not problem-solving as defined (a goal followed by figuring out a way to reach it). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 not satisfied; I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study is empirical, healthy-adult, and reports group-level whole-brain component analyses using BOLD fMRI (meets I6 and I8). However, it does not report a problem-solving task contrast that meets the review's definition of problem solving (I5 not met): while a Tower of London task is mentioned in methods/piloting, results do not present Tower-of-London (planning/problem-solving) task effects, and the reported results focus on tasks like n-back, MSIT, JLO, COWAT. Critically, the paper does not provide stereotactic peak coordinate results for task-related increases in Talairach or MNI space as voxelwise coordinate tables or peak coordinates (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults performing an Embedded Figures Task that requires a goal-directed search (find hidden shape), meeting the review's broad definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (random-effects across n=16 and fixed-effects for a subset), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activation foci, and reports BOLD results with voxelwise maps and figures. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that includes an explicit problem-solving task: the hard non-semantic phoneme-segmentation task is described by the authors as involving problem-solving and working memory demands (meets I5). The study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses using FLAME and cluster-thresholding (meets I6) and uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). The manuscript describes whole-brain contrasts and cluster results (with figures/contrasts referenced) and full-brain ROIs and coordinates are discussed/used, indicating stereotactic results are available in the article figures/tables (meets I7 and I9). The population is healthy adults and task effects are reported (satisfying the review scope). Although the primary focus is semantic control, the inclusion of an explicitly problem-solving non-semantic task satisfies the meta-analysis objective. Confidence is moderate (0.7) because the provided full text excerpt does not display coordinate tables or figures explicitly, but the body text indicates whole-brain cluster results and ROI coordinates are reported elsewhere in the article.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using BOLD contrast (fMRI) and whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses. The tasks involve explicit goals and require participants to figure out selections/strategies to reach or maintain goal states (e.g., managing cumulative fish stocks within bounds; collecting shapes to match a target), meeting the review definition of problem solving (I5). The methods describe whole-brain normalization to the standard SPM EPI template (MNI) and second-level group analyses with FWE-corrected voxelwise results; results reference activation tables/figures, indicating stereotactic coordinate reporting typical of SPM outputs (I6–I9). All exclusion criteria do not apply (no ROI-only reporting, no clinical/group-only contrasts, empirical study). Confidence lowered slightly because coordinate tables themselves are referenced but not shown in the provided excerpt.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults but does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review (a goal with a need to figure out a way to reach it). It instead studies theory-of-mind/self-perspective inhibition using movie clips and stop-signal tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult subjects), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/peak coordinates reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not address the target cognitive domain (problem-solving).

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of arithmetic problem solving including healthy adults and children and reports group-level adult results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (arithmetic problem solving satisfies problem-solving definition), I6 (group-level effects in healthy adult participants using task fMRI/GLM), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the main text, figures, or visible tables; criterion I7 is not satisfied based on the material given. Although the paper refers to Supplementary Information, no explicit coordinate tables are present in the provided content and the allowance in I9 (that coordinates may be in supplementary materials) cannot be confirmed here. Per screening rules, ALL inclusion criteria must be met; because I7 is not demonstrated in the provided full text, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the supplied content.

This is a task-based BOLD-fMRI study of two-digit mental addition (choice-reaction), which meets the review's problem-solving definition (a goal to indicate the correct result and the need to compute/figure out the result). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants (N=16 after exclusion), normalized to MNI space, and provides voxelwise stereotactic coordinates and parametric contrasts. BOLD signal (fMRI) analyses are reported, with tables/figures and detailed voxelwise results. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study does not meet the review’s core eligibility. It is an fMRI task study with whole-brain MNI coordinates and BOLD analyses (satisfies I7, I8, I9). However, it does not study a problem-solving task as defined (task is letter/location discrimination, not goal-directed problem solving) and participants are male adolescents (ages 11–16) including an ADHD clinical group rather than healthy adults (fails I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (pyramid problems) in healthy adult participants that examines neural activity during problem solution and learning. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses (exploratory voxelwise contrasts identifying metacognitive and cognitive regions) and predefined ROI and whole-brain results. Stereotactic Talairach coordinates are reported for predefined regions and exploratory loci. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are described and presented in figures/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space; however the experimental task targets prospective memory (performing real-world errands in VR) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (explicitly requiring subjects to formulate and figure out ways to reach a goal). Although the VR PM task involves goal-directed behavior and navigation, the paper frames and analyzes processes as prospective memory components (intention maintenance, target detection, action, switching) rather than domain-general problem solving. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not met, while I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study administered the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), which requires establishing a goal (match cards) and discovering/adjusting rules to reach it, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses for healthy adult controls (single-group results and group comparisons) (I6). Task-related increases are reported as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables/figures referenced; z coordinate of Talairach space noted) (I7). BOLD fMRI was used and analyzed (I8). Voxelwise and clusterwise results are presented in tables and figures in the main text, consistent with acceptable reporting (I9). Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results, but it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a task with an explicit goal that requires figuring out a way to reach it). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task; it examines sentential negation/language comprehension). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-only or between-group-only contrasts, empirical data present). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I5.

This empirical task-based fMRI study includes the Tower of London task, a canonical problem-solving/planning paradigm (I5). It reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (normalized to MNI space) with task-related activation maps and contrasts (whole-brain FDR-corrected maps), and provides region coordinates (e.g., caudate coordinates) and post hoc group comparisons involving healthy controls (fulfilling I6 and I7). BOLD fMRI was used (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text (I9). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, and is sufficiently complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI results (it includes whole-brain SPM), is not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore it is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain, task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This study is excluded because it reports only an a priori ROI analysis rather than whole-brain stereotactic coordinate results (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a working-memory n-Back, which does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task), I6 (no clear whole-brain group-level coordinate-based analysis is reported — results are presented from ROIs), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases are reported in the text), I9 (no coordinates in main text, tables, figures or supplement are provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using problem-solving tasks (NSI and OSI) where participants had a goal and had to figure out methods to reach it (I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects GLM analyses in healthy university adults (I6), with results transformed into Talairach space and peak coordinates reported (I7). BOLD fMRI was used and analyzed (I8). Voxelwise task effects and coordinates are reported in figures/tables and correlations with behavior are presented (I9). The study does not rely solely on ROIs, does not report only group comparisons of disease/age/gender, and includes healthy-group task effects, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (multi-digit addition), which constitutes a problem-solving task (goal-directed computation). It reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group comparisons only, empirical healthy-sample task effects present).

Exclusion: E3 and E5. The study is an fMRI BOLD study (I8 met) but does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met), does not report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults (I6 not met), and does not report stereotactic coordinates from a whole-brain analysis (I7 not met). Instead, the analysis is restricted to pre-defined regions of interest (ROI-only analysis), and results are presented as ROI BOLD magnitudes rather than voxelwise whole-brain coordinates (meets exclusion E3). The paper focuses on bipolar patients with lithium treatment and lacks a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (meets exclusion E5). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, (I9 not applicable). Therefore the study should be excluded from the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study of chess problem solving (deliberative checkmate problems) in healthy adult participants (GM/M and novices). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses and between-group comparisons, provides task-related activation/deactivation results with MNI stereotactic coordinates, and uses BOLD fMRI (resting-state and task runs). Voxelwise results and maps/coordinates are presented in the text and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults reporting whole-brain group analyses and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results. However, the experimental task is a working memory manipulation (reordering four letters following a cue) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (a goal plus a need to figure out a way to reach it in a problem-solving context). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text is a complete, empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). However, the experimental task is a working-memory maintenance/manipulation delayed-response paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal plus need to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The study is excluded solely because it does not investigate problem-solving as required by the review.

This study is an fMRI investigation of financial decision-making under risk, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal followed by the need to figure out a way to reach it). While it includes healthy adults and whole-brain group analyses and BOLD fMRI, the task is choice-based (lottery vs. sure win with expert advice) rather than problem-solving across domains. Additionally, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) in the content supplied here, so I7 is not clearly met based on the provided material. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria (I5 and I7) and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using arithmetic problem-solving (subtraction) tasks; includes whole-brain analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) with BOLD fMRI results. Meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria met.

The study used a mathematical/arithmetic series task requiring participants to infer a rule and select the next number—an explicit problem-solving paradigm (I5). It is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=12) with group-level random-effects analyses (I6). Data were normalized to Talairach coordinates and stereotactic results/ROIs are reported (I7). The paper reports both BOLD and CBF (ASL) analyses and derives CMRO2 (I8). Whole-brain voxelwise activation/deactivation maps and coordinates are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to between-group or clinical comparisons, and this is empirical human data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and reports a task-based BOLD fMRI whole-brain study in healthy adults (Experiment 2). However, the experimental task is a number magnitude comparison/selection task (choose larger or smaller number based on a cue) that manipulates symbolic distance and cognitive effort. This does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5), which requires goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical thinking to arrive at a correct or novel solution. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results reported in main text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied; full text is complete.

Full text is complete. While the study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation with healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in Talairach space, it does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review. The tasks are reading/naming and parity (odd/even) judgments—rapid perceptual/semantic decisions that do not require planning, sequencing, or generation of solutions to a novel goal-directed problem. Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I5.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental task is a simple number-estimation/perceptual decision (judge whether number of dots is higher/lower than a figure) and does not involve goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing of actions, or critical-thinking operations as required by I5. However, the study does meet other inclusion criteria: it reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise results in text/figures/ROIs (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not a patient-group-only comparison, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded for failing I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a clear problem-solving task (the rule-finding task requires forming hypotheses, evaluating feedback, and discovering an unknown arithmetic rule), satisfying I5. Participants were healthy adult volunteers and group-level whole-brain analyses were reported (preprocessing, GLM, group subtraction analyses), satisfying I6. Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates, with Talairach conversions) satisfying I7. The study reports BOLD (fMRI) analyses throughout satisfying I8. Voxelwise/whole-brain subtraction and PPI results are reported and described in the main text and figures, satisfying I9. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a methods/review paper describing a single-scan dynamic molecular imaging PET technique and summarizing prior task-based PET findings. It is not an original empirical PET/fMRI study that examines problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations within a rule set). It does not report whole-brain, group-level stereotactic coordinate results for a problem-solving task in healthy adults, nor does it report BOLD or rCBF analyses. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original human problem-solving data). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults specific to problem-solving), I7 (stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD/rCBF analysis). No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study is an fMRI investigation of neural responses to advantageous and disadvantageous inequity using a perceptual discrimination and reward-feedback task. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports peak coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a perceptual judgment with monetary feedback and social comparison, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing operations to arrive at a solution as defined by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD analyses and stereotactic (MNI) results, the experimental tasks (Flanker, False Belief, attention/working memory, and Monetary Incentive Delay) do not constitute problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed operations requiring critical thinking/planning/sequencing to find solutions within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, or similar rule frameworks). Hence inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Tower of London task, which is a canonical problem-solving/planning task (goal-directed planning and sequencing). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with task effects across and within healthy groups, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are reported and an ROI analysis was supplementary to whole-brain results. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is an n-back working memory paradigm (updating/maintenance), which does not fit the review's defined problem-solving tasks (goal-directed planning/sequencing to derive novel solutions). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results registered/reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/cluster results available in figures/maps). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports BOLD whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates and group-level effects related to BDNF genotype. However, the experimental paradigms are virtual navigation and memory strategy tasks (4/8VM and CSDLT) aimed at dissociating hippocampus- versus caudate-dependent navigational strategies and memory-system recruitment. These tasks do not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5), which requires tasks designed around goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing under explicit rule sets (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving). Although navigation involves goal-directed behavior and sequencing, the study’s focus is spatial memory/strategy selection rather than domain-general or domain-specific problem solving as defined. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates and voxelwise results. However, the cognitive tasks used are finger-tapping (motor) and a mental rotation task (visuospatial discrimination). Mental rotation is a perceptual/visuospatial transformation task and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-driven planning/sequencing/critical evaluation to derive a solution under a rule set). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis), I7 (Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results shown in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is a methods paper using MEG–fMRI fusion with simulations and a single-subject visual checkerboard experiment, not a task-based problem-solving study. It does include BOLD/fMRI analyses but does not provide whole-brain, group-level task effects in healthy adults nor stereotactic coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analysis is ROI-based/single-ROI rather than whole-brain voxelwise reporting) and E5 (no healthy-group, group-level task effect — single-subject data only). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

This study was excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a rule-switching/stimulus-response (SR) mapping paradigm examining cognitive control and effector modality (saccade vs. manual) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring participants to identify/plan novel solutions across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or other domains. It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise stereotactic results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task qualifies as problem-solving — Wisconsin Card Sorting Task requires identifying/implementing changing sorting rules, planning/sequence and set-shifting), I6 (whole-brain, data-driven functional network analysis with group-level effects reported both in healthy controls (Experiment 1) and in control group comparisons), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis reported). I9 is also satisfied insofar as voxelwise, whole-brain network results are presented in figures and AAL-based mappings. Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the paper does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI peak coordinates/tables) for task activations/contrasts. The analyses are presented as network maps, histograms, and AAL-region percentages but no standardized coordinate tables or peak coordinates are provided. Because I7 is required, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study uses a rule-switching task that requires participants to identify and apply task rules to reach correct responses (goal-directed, rule-based operations in bivalent/univalent trials), which meets the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants (n=20), with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 24 20 18) reported and FWE-corrected results; voxelwise results are described in text and figures. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study uses a complex working memory (reading/listening span) task rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined in the protocol. While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and reports voxelwise results, it does not examine problem solving (planning/sequencing/deriving novel solutions) across domains. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task (sentence–picture matching with feedback to bias spatial frame-of-reference interpretations) does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task. The task lacks a clear goal requiring participants to devise or plan actions or perform critical-thinking processes to generate a previously unknown solution (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a goal-directed virtual maze requiring subjects to plan and sequence actions to find a hidden goal, meeting the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy control task effects (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., 18 -61 40) (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results and activation maps are reported in the full text (I9). It is not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical human fMRI data, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used a prolonged visual search task (perceptual/attention/fatigue paradigm) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning, or rule-based solution processes were assessed). The full text contains whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults and reports BOLD results (satisfying I6 and I8). The manuscript refers to activation tables/figures, so voxelwise results are indicated as available (I9). However, stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space are not clearly reported in the provided full text (I7 not confirmed). Therefore the key inclusion criterion I5 is not met, leading to exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The Hayling sentence completion test is a verbal initiation/fluency and executive control task probing semantic completion and response initiation/inhibition, but it does not clearly embody the review’s specified problem-solving construct (a goal-driven requirement to evaluate, plan/sequence actions and execute operations within a rule set to reach a previously unknown solution). The paper does meet other technical criteria: it reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult participants (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and presents voxelwise results in the text/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, nor non-empirical). Therefore it must be excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5.

This study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5. The Kana Pick-out Test (KPT) is a dual-task assessing divided attention, working memory, reading and vowel detection, not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing or applying rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task), I7 (the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space), and I9 (no coordinates/tables/figures with stereotactic results are present in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation (BOLD) that reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and includes healthy adult participants and group-level analyses; however, the experimental task is a probabilistic reversal learning paradigm focused on reinforcement learning and cognitive flexibility, not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks to derive a solution). Therefore it fails to meet I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. It uses the Eriksen flanker task to study error recognition, reconcentration, and post-error adjustment (conflict monitoring/response selection), which does not involve setting a goal and devising/planning a novel sequence of operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore EXCLUDED for the meta-analysis because it fails I5.

This PET study used [11C]-raclopride binding during a probabilistic classification (weather prediction) task in healthy adults. It does not meet the review’s requirements: it reports only ROI-based PET binding analyses rather than whole-brain, voxelwise results, and therefore violates exclusion E3. It also fails multiple inclusion criteria: I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate tables/voxelwise coordinates reported), and I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF measures — it reports neurotransmitter binding PET). Additionally, the task is a probabilistic classification/learning paradigm (incidental feedback-based learning), which is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined by I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study investigates perceptual decision-making (detection of an animal among distractors) and how motivation shifts response bias, using event-related fMRI. It does not examine problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions or critical thinking processes to arrive at a correct/new solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The study does meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6); reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7); reports BOLD analyses (I8); and voxelwise results are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it fails I5 (does not study problem-solving).

This is an fMRI study of number notation usage using number comparison and digit identification tasks in healthy adult binumerates. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates reported), it does not examine 'problem-solving' as defined by the review (goal-driven tasks requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The tasks are magnitude comparison and digit identification (perceptual/semantic/automaticity judgments) rather than problem-solving/critical-thinking tasks. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Met inclusion criteria: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is a methods paper using real-time fMRI and SPRT, applied to face vs. house perception and simulations; it does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (I5 not met). The empirical real-data example is a single-subject/ROI-focused FFA analysis rather than a whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6 not met). The paper reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8 met). It appears analyses focus on an ROI (mask of 717 voxels) and comparisons within that ROI rather than whole-brain voxelwise, and results are presented as ROI maps rather than providing stereotactic coordinate tables for whole-brain group effects; thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Summary: Excluded because E3 applies; inclusion criteria met: I8; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/tables/figures available). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5. The experimental task is a probability-learning and decision-making paradigm (learning color–payoff associations and choosing gambles). While it involves inference and maximizing reward, it does not constitute a problem-solving task as defined for the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel or correct solution across domains). Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis’ core inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study used task-based BOLD fMRI of a virtual radial arm maze requiring goal-directed navigation, memory, planning and decision-making (meets I5). It reports BOLD analyses (meets I8) in healthy adult participants. However, all reported analyses are ROI-based multivariate results rather than whole-brain voxelwise, group-level stereotactic coordinate results. It does not present whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses nor report activation coordinates in Talairach/MNI space, thus failing I6 and I7. Because the paper reports only ROI results, exclusion criterion E3 is met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations to arrive at a solution). Instead, it investigates event simulation, situational inference, and future-prediction processes. The full text meets other inclusion criteria: I6 (task-based whole-brain fMRI with group-level analysis in healthy adults, N=20), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I5.

The study is an fMRI investigation of semantic memory/semantic judgments (same/different color or shape of word pairs). While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with MNI coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) of task-related activations, which fails inclusion criterion I7. The paper does satisfy that it uses a task-based semantic decision paradigm consistent with a semantic problem-solving framework (I5), includes whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6), and reports BOLD-based functional connectivity analyses (I8). However, it does not provide coordinates (I7) and does not provide stereotactic voxelwise coordinate results in text/tables/supplementary materials (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study does not examine problem-solving tasks as defined in the review. It investigates spontaneous thought and offline memory reprocessing (resting-state and a memory-recall condition) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations to reach an external goal or apply rule-based problem solving. The paper does satisfy several technical criteria (whole-brain group-level BOLD fMRI analysis in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates), but it fails inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review). The tasks used are spatial learning, viewpoint-shift and path-integration training and memory-based virtual maze encoding/retrieval; these are spatial memory/navigation tasks rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution under a delimited rule set. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of problem-solving task activations.

This study uses a reward-based instrumental learning task (visual cues and auditory feedback) focused on credit assignment and reward outcome signalling in sensory cortex, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem formulation/critical thinking/planning/sequencing operations to arrive at novel solutions). Additionally, the fMRI acquisition was a partial-volume (48 mm) coverage targeted at visual cortex and reward-related regions rather than whole-brain coverage; thus it does not include a whole-brain group-level analysis as required. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain analysis/group-level whole-brain effects). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly applicable.

The study uses a task-based BOLD fMRI PVSAT paradigm (subjects perform serial addition rules) which meets the review's problem-solving definition (execution of arithmetic operations according to a rule set). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activations for healthy controls (one-sample t-tests) and between-group random-effects analyses. Images were normalized to MNI space and activation peak coordinates are reported, and BOLD fMRI was used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion, so content is complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults (Talairach normalization reported) and associated coordinate results, but it does not investigate problem solving as defined by the review. The tasks are perceptual/semantic action-observation judgments (space: orientation matching; function: compatibility of tool and object) rather than goal-directed problem-solving that requires planning/sequencing or discovering solutions. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), an affective decision-making task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution). It does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and the text indicates voxelwise results/cluster tables/figures are available (I9). However, the core content does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).
